title: MAJOR BUY! If You Missed Nvidia, This is Even Bigger
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue's video is about cybersecurity consolidation, not Nvidia — the title is a hook. The trigger is CrowdStrike's acquisition of Zscaler, announced over the weekend: 1.13 CRWD shares per ZS share, a $43.9bn deal worth about $260 per Zscaler share, a 33% premium, sending ZS up 17% on Monday. He argues cybersecurity has been the star of the year: the HACK ETF is up 50% in 2026 against under 8% for the AIQ AI ETF, and the group held up in the crash (down just 1.6% over the past month versus AIQ down almost 12%), because security budgets cannot be cut — the average data breach now costs over $5m — and Gartner forecasts cyber spending growing 68% to $86bn inside $4tn of global AI spending next year. Enterprise customers now want all-in-one platforms, driving consolidation. He then values four smaller pure-play names as next buyout candidates using the Zscaler deal terms (11.17x sales, 53x earnings): Okta, the identity-access leader with ~15% market share, target ~$208 per share; SentinelOne, ~20% growth but a -21% EBITDA margin and never GAAP-profitable, worth ~$11-12bn (~35% upside); Check Point, slow 4.3% growth but a 30% EBITDA margin, target ~$219 (~38% upside); and Rubrik, 32% growth but already 13x sales and 224x earnings, so a premium is likely too high to attract buyers. Calls: ZS BUY (reiterated, he has been buying), OKTA BUY (flip from HOLD), S CONDITIONAL_BUY (first tracked), CHKP BUY (first tracked), RBRK UNCERTAIN (first tracked). Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Fortinet are named as the buyers, too large to be acquired.

CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9B — 1.13 CRWD shares per ZS share, about $260 per share, a 33% premium. Cybersecurity is the star of the year: the HACK ETF is up 50% in 2026 vs under 8% for the AIQ AI ETF, and the group held up in the crash (down just 1.6% over the past month vs AIQ down almost 12%).

calls.bull: Consolidation spreads and the whole cyber group re-rates higher.
calls.bear: The deal breaks or the AI-threat spending wave slows.

calls.video_title: MAJOR BUY! If You Missed Nvidia, This is Even Bigger
calls.thesis: First tracked. SentinelOne is 'very attractively, very cheaply priced' on price-to-earnings adjusted for growth, with ~20% expected revenue growth — but he has never liked it and never owned shares because of the -21% EBITDA margin and no GAAP profit ever. On Zscaler deal terms (11x sales) it would be worth ~$13.4B market cap (~68% above the recent close); he puts buyout value closer to ~$11-12B (~35% higher) and says it is 'very likely to get some kind of a buyout offer eventually at this price'. Conditioned on the buyout thesis and the cheap valuation, not on the standalone business.
calls.base: A buyer pays ~$11-12B for the AI endpoint platform.
calls.bull: Full 11x-sales terms apply and it is worth ~$13.4B (~68% higher).
calls.bear: Losses persist, no buyer comes, and the cheap price proves deserved.
calls.price_at_call: Buyout value ~$11-12B market cap (~35% above recent close)

calls.thesis: First tracked. Check Point is worth a look on buyout maths: only ~4.3% expected revenue growth, but a 30% EBITDA margin (matched only by Fortinet in cyber). On a conservative 8x sales it would be a ~$22B market cap, ~40% above the recent price, or ~$219 per share at ~21x earnings — 'about a 38% upside and I think worth it' on the profitability, even though slow growth makes him hesitant.
calls.base: A buyer pays ~8x sales, ~$219 per share.
calls.bull: A buyer pays full Zscaler-style terms and the premium is larger.
calls.bear: Slow growth caps the multiple and no buyer pays up.
